sentences.text: Revenue rose from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025, a 26.0% CAGR [F1][F10][F231].
Operating margin moved from -8.6% to 10.7% over the same years, against a window high of 22.2% in FY2021 [F51][F60][D794].
Gross margin rose 10.8pp in FY2017, which the filing attributes mainly to the absence of a 2016 charge worth eight gross margin points [D53][P68].
Revenue rose 43.6% in FY2022 with the Xilinx acquisition, but operating margin fell 16.8pp to 5.4% as Xilinx-related amortization hit gross margin [D314][D330][F57][P46].
Client and Gaming contributed 19.0pp of FY2025's 34.3% revenue growth, and Data Center 15.7pp [D701][D483][D694].
Those two segments now make up most of revenue, with Data Center at 48.0% and Client and Gaming at 42.0% [D692][D699].
The filing credits Client unit shipments up 31% with prices up 15%, and Data Center demand for EPYC and Instinct products [P10][P13].
Operating income grew 94.4% on 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 20.3%, as operating expenses rose 24.3% [D484][D483][D511][D504].
Diluted EPS grew 165.0%, in line with net income's 164.2%, as the share count fell 0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Operating margin of 10.7% sits above its 7.2% window median but well below the 22.2% high [F60][D795][D794].
Among six semis peers it ranks at the 17th percentile, against a 31.0% peer median [D818][D819].
Gross margin of 49.5% is at its window high; the filing cites product mix, against about $440 million of export-control inventory charges [F40][D800][P14].
The FY2025 operating margin gain of 3.3pp came partly from other lines (+2.6pp), alongside a $140 million fall in acquisition amortization [D499][D516][P7].
Net margin of 12.5% sits 1.8pp above operating margin, helped by $577 million of unrealized investment gains and an $853 million tax release [F80][F60][X123][P5][P4].
Free cash flow was 1.55x net income against a 1.17x window median, and operating cash flow 1.78x, including $1.2 billion from discontinued operations [D471][D810][D470][P3].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% is near the 19.6% window high and far above the 6.5% median [D467][D803][D804].
Working capital absorbed $2.4 billion, mainly a $2.2 billion inventory build for Data Center ramps [P3].
Capex rose 53.1% to $974 million, 1.87x depreciation and amortization [D490][F120][D472].
Net cash of $6.46 billion is 18.6% of revenue, the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a -13.9% median [D476][D477][D826][D827].
Total debt rose 138.0% to $4.10 billion after $1.5 billion of notes issued in March 2025 [D508][D475][P6].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion used 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [X150][D479][D506].
The cash cushion is still large, but gross debt is rising again after two years of repayments [X161][X162][D508].
Inventory days have risen each year since FY2021, from 84 to 165, and inventory grew 38.1% to $7.92 billion in FY2025 [D256][D481][D510][X203].
The filing ties the $2.2 billion build to Data Center ramps in advanced process nodes [P3].
Total debt rose 138.0% to $4.10 billion in FY2025, a medium-severity flag, with net cash still at $6.46 billion [D508][D475][D476].
Operating income was $3.69 billion but net income $4.34 billion, helped by an $853 million tax release and $577 million other income [F50][F70][P4][X123][P5].
Inventory days below the FY2023 level of 130 [D368] would confirm the build is unwinding; above 165 [D481] would extend the flag in the FY2026 10-K.
A free cash flow margin falling toward the 6.5% window median [D804] from 19.4% [D467] would show FY2025 conversion is not durable, in the FY2026 10-K.
Net cash below the FY2025 level of $6.46 billion [D476] would show the new borrowing eroding the balance sheet, in the FY2026 10-K.
